video.title: Portland Trail Blazers 2026/27 NBA Season Preview: Too Many Guards & Too Much Usage

summary: Josh Lloyd and Mike Richmond (Locked On Blazers) preview the 2026/27 Portland Trail Blazers. The roster is crowded with guards (Lillard, Morant, Holiday, Henderson, Sharpe) and with centers, and it is short on forwards after Jerami Grant, Kris Murray, Matisse Thybulle and others left. The projected starting five is Lillard, Morant, Camara, Avdija and Clingan. Holiday, Sharpe and Henderson are expected to come off the bench except when Morant or Lillard are out. Both expect Avdija's usage and output to drop, Lillard to play around 30 minutes, and Clingan to stay at about 28 minutes with no big leap. The fantasy takeaway is that minutes and usage on this team will be volatile, so managers should not count on these players for reliability. Mike predicts about 44 wins.

rules.text: When a team adds several high-usage players, project their usage down. Not everyone can keep last season's usage because there is only one ball.
rules.quote: there's only so many balls and this is the highest group of usage players all to put in

rules.text: If you add up past-season usage for a crowded roster without regressing it, the team projection becomes unrealistic. You have to bring every player's numbers down.
rules.quote: the team was running with like a pace at like 130 possessions a game if I didn't start bringing all the usage numbers down

rules.text: On crowded rosters where minutes and usage swing from game to game, do not overvalue players for reliability.
rules.quote: we can't overindex on these guys for reliability because there's going to be a lot of ups and downs

rules.text: A player's lower efficiency can bounce back when his usage is reduced.
rules.quote: Maybe the reduction in usage brings him back.

team_notes.text: Expected to stagger Lillard and Morant but still close games with both. Transition defense is projected to be poor, and offensive rebounding got worse.

team_notes.text: Expect minutes and usage to swing from game to game across the rotation. The speaker doubts a consolidation trade.
